newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rose to 11.9 pct vs 10.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rose to 11.9 pct vs 10.9 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate rose one percentage point to 11.9 percent in lively trade on Friday, dealers said.
Settlements totalled 34.6 million kuna on a good supply of 50 million. Fresh loans accounted for most of the day's trade.
Weighted call money rate rose to 11.2 percent from 10.5 percent, pushed up by a single 12 percent deal by a savings bank.

Insurers rolled over one-week loans at the usual 9 percent rate, while banks extended two-week funds at 13 and 14 percent. Single one-month loan, borrowed by a savings bank, was renewed at 16 percent.
The central bank's kuna mid-rates for Saturday were slightly firmer at 6.0132 against the dollar and weaker at 3.5657 against the German mark.
